headline: The European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology has signed a joint statement on the revision of EU medical device rules and says it backs building AI Act requirements into them instead of adding a second layer.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: short position statement, read in full; no decision or rule change yet.
importance_line: Cancer patients and radiation oncology clinics could get AI tools sooner if the rule sets are merged, which also matters to regulators and device makers, but this is an industry position statement, not a decision, and the post does not list the other signers.
summary: ESTRO, the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology, said in a LinkedIn post, reproduced by Oncodaily, that it has joined MedTech Europe, the European medical technology industry body, and partner health organisations in a joint statement on the ongoing revision of the EU Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostics Regulation (IVDR). It supports one streamlined pathway that builds the AI Act's requirements into those regulations, which it says would avoid double regulation, keep safety standards high and speed patient access to AI tools.
notes: Source is ESTRO (its own LinkedIn post); the link is Oncodaily's page where the text was read.
